domain_restrictions: A and B must be nonzero polynomials so that their degrees are defined and the quotient is meaningful as a rational function.
A and B lie in the polynomial ring with integer coefficients in q.
The hypothesis that A divided by B is itself a polynomial means the rational function has no remaining denominator after simplification and is an element of the same polynomial ring.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every pair of nonzero integer coefficient polynomials A and B in q, if A divided by B is a polynomial in q, then degree of A is at least degree of B.
quantifier_order: For all polynomials A and B with integer coefficients in q, assuming both are nonzero, if the quotient A divided by B is itself a polynomial with integer coefficients in q, then the degree of A is at least the degree of B.

variables.domain: polynomials with integer coefficients in q
variables.name: A

variables.domain: polynomials with integer coefficients in q
variables.name: B

witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses in the statement.
The conclusion depends only on the pair A, B and the assumption that the quotient belongs to the polynomial ring.

statement_nl: Let A(q) and B(q) be nonzero polynomials in Z[q]. If the rational function A(q) / B(q) is itself a polynomial in Z[q], then deg(A) >= deg(B).
